exercise.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
library_steps: Sit on a bench and set the front of one foot on a block.
Rest a dumbbell on that knee and hold it in place.
Raise your heel as high as you can, then lower slowly.
Finish your reps, then switch legs.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated, knee bent ~90 deg, ball of one foot on an 8 cm block with the heel hanging off; heel drops ~15 deg below the block then rises ~30 deg (ankle only, knee angle unchanged) while the hand holds a dumbbell across that knee. Soleus (calves) is the target.

setup.target: Sit tall on a bench, working knee bent about 90 deg, shin near vertical.
setup.why: With the knee bent the gastrocnemius is shortened and the soleus does more of the work.

setup.target: Ball of the foot on the block edge, heel hanging off behind it.
setup.why: Lets the heel drop below the block for full range.

setup.target: Dumbbell lies across the lower thigh just behind the knee, held with the hand.
setup.why: Loads the calf through the knee; library setup.

setup.target: Foot flat on the floor, relaxed.

movement.measure: 0 = foot square to the shin; - = heel down (dorsiflexion), + = heel up (plantarflexion)

movement.end: ~90 deg (thigh lifts with the heel; knee angle unchanged)

movement.measure: stay still (hand rides up with the knee)

muscles.emg: Knee flexed 90 deg: medial gastrocnemius EMG ~35% lower than knee straight, soleus same or up to 15-28% higher at slow speeds (S1). Seated version 'mostly trains the soleus' (S2).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Heel never drops below the block or rises only a little.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Study range was 15 deg dorsiflexion to 30 deg plantarflexion; short reps lose most of it.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Thigh lifted by the hip or arms instead of the ankle.

sources.citation: Kovacs B, Csala D, Yang S, Tihanyi J, Gu Y, Hortobagyi T. 2024. Knee position affects medial gastrocnemius and soleus activation during dynamic plantarflexion: no evidence for an inter-muscle compensation in healthy young adults. Biology Open 13(12):bio061810.
sources.what_it_gave: n=30; knee 0 vs 90 deg; plantarflexion from 15 deg dorsiflexion to 30 deg plantarflexion. Knee-flexed: torque -31%, medial gastrocnemius EMG -35%, soleus +15-28% early in slow reps.

sources.citation: StrengthLog. How to do seated calf raise: muscles worked and proper form.
sources.what_it_gave: Toes and ball of the foot on the support; lower with a controlled ankle bend, push up by extending the ankles; mostly trains the soleus because the gastrocnemius is shortened.

clip_check.check: Start: working heel below the block
End: heel high, ball of foot still on the block (not sliding)
Forefoot rests on block top (no float, no sink)
Other foot flat on the floor
Dumbbell rests on the lower thigh, hand on handle
Calf strongest red in both pictures
